newsitem.title: INDIA: Seven killed in India train blast - police.
newsitem.headline: Seven killed in India train blast - police.

text.p: Seven people were killed and eight injured on Thursday when a bomb planted by suspected separatist militants exploded on a train track in northeastern India, derailing a passenger carriage, police said.
They said the blast occurred in North Lakahimpur district in Assam state, about 200 km (120 miles) east of the region's largest city Guwahati.
Police in Guwahati said 70 to 80 passengers were in the last carriage of the local train when the device went off on the tracks.

Authorities said they had yet to identify those who set off the explosion but they suspected the United Liberation Front of Assam, one of several separatist groups in the state. Officials have said they expected a surge in violence in connection with the 50th anniversary of India's independence this week.
On Monday, more than 400 passengers escaped unhurt when tribal guerrillas set off a remote-control bomb on a rail track in Assam.
Tribal guerrillas on Tuesday killed 12 Hindus, executing six after tying them to a tree, in a series of attacks on villages in Assam.
